ICYMI O/N

Man City bottled the league. 

IRAN:

US President Trump said in a Salem News interview, “time is not of the essence for us” in making a deal with Iran. “Probably another two weeks...maybe three weeks,” Trump said the Iran war could go on for. (Salem News via BBG)

Trump wants to avoid a fresh bombing campaign, officials said to the WSJ, preferring a negotiated end to Tehran’s nuclear advancements and the weekslong war. However, he is currently debating between either a military or diplomatic path forward. Some US and foreign officials said they believed Trump was likely to authorize a military response to Iran within days. (WSJ)

The Iranian attack on the UAE, Oman, and in the Straight of Hormuz was done by the IRGC without the knowledge or coordination of the Iranian government. Iranian President Pezeshkian is "extremely angry" at the actions of Ahmad Vahidi, the commander of the IRGC, and has called for an urgent meeting to stop attacks on Persian Gulf countries. (Iran International)

Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi posted "As talks are making progress with Pakistan's gracious effort, the US should be wary of being dragged back into quagmire by ill-wishers. So should the UAE." HE added, "Events in Hormuz make clear that there's no military solution to a political crisis." (X)

Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, said in a social media post on Tuesday that the security of shipping and energy transit had been threatened by breaches of the four-week-old ceasefire by the U.S. and its allies. (RTRS)

US intelligence assessments indicate that the time Iran would need to build a nuclear weapon has not changed since last summer, when analysts estimated that a U.S.-Israeli attack had pushed back the timeline to up to a year, according to Reuters sources. The unchanged timeline suggests that significantly impeding Tehran's nuclear program may require destroying or removing Iran's remaining stockpile of highly enriched uranium. (RTRS)

Two U.S. Navy destroyers transited the Strait of Hormuz and entered the Persian Gulf after navigating an Iranian barrage consisting of small boats, missiles and drones, according to defense officials who spoke to CBS News on Monday. Despite the intensity of the attacks, neither U.S. vessel was struck, according to the officials. (CBS)

An Iranian commander denied that the US destroyed Iranian attack boats on Monday and gave an alternate version of events. The commander was quoted by Iran’s state broadcaster, IRIB, as saying that the US hit two small cargo boats crossing the Strait of Hormuz to Iran from Oman and killed five civilians aboard. (WSJ)

Explosions were heard during the night in the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas and on Qassem Island in the Persian Gulf according to an Israeli journalist. (N12 via Telegram)

South Korea confirmed that a cargo ship in the Persian Gulf operated by a Korean company suffered damage but didn’t immediately respond to President Trump’s suggestion that it might be time for Seoul to “come and join the mission” in the Strait of Hormuz. (WSJ)

Hundreds of vessels were seen clustering near Dubai on Tuesday, as more ships moved away from a still-empty Strait of Hormuz in response to Iran’s efforts to widen its area of control. (BBG)

ENERGY CRISIS:

The Philippines is the latest developing nation to see inflation jump because of the Mideast conflict. Consumer prices rose 7.2% in April Y/Y, the fastest pace since March 2023 and a big step up from March’s 4.1% increase. Higher rice prices were a top contributor to inflation, showing how higher energy costs are spreading into the rest of the economy. (WSJ)

Thailand’s government plans to raise 400 billion baht ($12 billion) in new debt to support farmers, low-income households, and small businesses affected by the fallout from the Middle East conflict, while accelerating the country’s shift away from fossil fuels. (BBG)

Iraq is offering its term buyers huge discounts for crude loaded this month, but tankers will have to transit the Strait of Hormuz to collect the barrels deep inside the Persian Gulf just as hostilities flare in the region. (BBG)

Russia’s Kirishi oil refinery near the Baltic coast is on fire after overnight drone strikes, according to NASA satellite images, as Ukraine ramps up attacks ahead of planned Victory Day ceasefires. (BBG)

Diamondback Energy Inc., one of the biggest shale oil producers, is boosting crude output in response to rising prices caused by the Iran war. (BBG)

Qantas Airways Ltd. Chief Executive Officer Vanessa Hudson said she has turned more upbeat about jet fuel availability, a fresh sign of optimism among aviation leaders as the Iran war upends energy markets. (BBG)

India's Petronet LNG expects Qatar to resume operations at its liquefied natural gas facilities within three to four weeks of the Middle East crisis ending, its head of finance, Saurav Mitra, said during an analyst call on Tuesday. (RTRS)

MACRO:

US President Trump said he will raise the case of Hong Kong’s imprisoned former media tycoon Jimmy Lai in his upcoming summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, adding a potential friction point to an agenda already complicated by the Iran war. (BBG)

China is slowing its efforts to repatriate Chinese nationals who are in the U.S. illegally, a senior Trump administration official told Reuters, warning that Washington was prepared to increase travel restrictions on the country if Beijing didn't reverse course. (RTRS)

PIMCO's international clients are seeking to diversify away from US markets amid geopolitical shifts and as a prolonged equity rally increases their exposure to the world’s largest market, according to Christian Stracke, the company’s president. (BBG)

Japan can conduct only two more sessions of three-day interventions by November if it wants to maintain its status of having a freely floating exchange rate, based on International Monetary Fund guidelines. (BBG)

The EU has tools that it can turn to if Donald Trump makes excessive threats to strategic industries such as steel, French Trade Minister Nicolas Forissier said. (BBG)

Labour MPs are discussing plans to demand UK PM Starmer set a date for his resignation in a letter inspired by the putsch by Gordon Brown’s allies against Tony Blair in 2006. (The Times)

US Treasury Secretary Bessent had a fierce row with UK Chancellor Reeves in Washington last month over her outspoken criticism of the Iran war, according to FT sources. (FT)

UK PM Starmer must embrace “taxing for growth” and an expansion of state-subsidised jobs to improve living standards, a member of his government has argued. (FT)

The UK Treasury and DMO said it will introduce a 12-month T-bill at weekly tenders by the end of the 2026-27 financial year. The new maturity is designed to “capture incremental sources of structural demand for maturities beyond six months,” according to a statement Tuesday. (DMO)

Angela Rayner held private talks with Al Carns, the armed forces minister, to shore up her credentials on defence policy before a Labour leadership race. (The Times)

Switzerland’s inflation quickened to a 16-month high in April as energy costs jumped because of war in the Middle East. (BBG)

The RBA raised its key interest rate for a third consecutive meeting, with Governor Michele Bullock signaling policymakers would now pause to assess its next steps. Traders trimmed expectations of rate hikes after Bullock’s comments Tuesday, with the market pricing just one more increase in the third quarter. (BBG)

Australian household spending rose at its fastest pace in two years in March, driven by a spike in gasoline prices following the outbreak of war in Iran and complicating the Reserve Bank’s efforts to cool the economy. (BBG)

South Korean Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan will meet U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick this week to discuss Korean investment in the United States, Seoul said, as part of steps to implement a trade deal the countries signed last year. (RTRS)

Indonesia’s central bank intervened in the foreign-exchange markets as the rupiah set a new record low. (BBG)

Indonesia’s economic growth accelerated to a three-year high in the first quarter, as a record increase in government spending helped support consumers in the face of a global energy crisis. (BBG)

Mexxican President Sheinbaum’s government unveiled plans meant to increase private investment into Mexico as she seeks to kickstart an economy that contracted to start the year. (BBG)

'Argentina’s Javier Milei battered by scandals and slowing economy' FT article notes President’s popularity falls as officials face graft allegations and unemployment climbs. (FT)

Romanian lawmakers will vote on ousting Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan in a move that could plunge the country into a renewed political crisis and imperil efforts to narrow the widest budget deficit in the European Union. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

Ukrainian drones are regularly hitting targets deep inside Russia, reaching to the Ural Mountains and communities where most people had seen the war as a distant problem. (BBG)

EQUITIES:

Apple has held exploratory discussions about using Intel (+2.8%) and Samsung Electronics (+5.4%) to produce the main processors for its devices in the US, a move that would offer a secondary option beyond longtime partner Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (BBG)

Intel has placed big orders for advanced packaging production line equipment to firms in Taiwan, media report, citing unnamed supply chain sources, and adding the equipment is for capacity expansion in Intel plants in Oregon and Vietnam. (Taiwan media via @dnystedt)

Palantir Technologies (-2%) soared to record quarterly revenue and profit in earnings reported on Monday, boosted by strong U.S. military demand and a rapidly growing business selling data-crunching software to American corporations. (WSJ)

OpenAI appears to be fast-tracking its first AI agent phone, with mass production targeted as early as 1H27. MediaTek currently appears better positioned to become the sole processor supplier, with the device set to use a customized version of the Dimensity 9600, built on TSMC’s N2P node in 2H26. (Ming-Chi Kuo)

IBM CEO Arvind Krishna says maximizing returns on investment in artificial intelligence requires a fundamental restructuring of business workflows rather than just adopting new technology. (WSJ)

Pinterest (+16%) posted double-digit growth in sales in the first quarter along with an increase in monthly users. (WSJ)

Meta Platforms Inc. is working on a financing package for a data center in El Paso, Texas, that could total roughly $13 billion, underscoring Big Tech’s growing reliance on debt to bankroll the infrastructure behind the AI boom. (BBG)

Alphabet Inc. has kicked off its latest megabond deal as it returns to the euro market just months after selling nearly $32 billion of dollar, sterling and Swiss franc-denominated debt. (BBG)

ServiceNow Inc. projected it would generate $30 billion of subscription revenue in 2030, attributing the strong outlook to traction from its AI products. (BBG)

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has projected confidence that the EU will soon green-light the carmaker's "Full Self-Driving" (FSD) system, but emails from some European regulators show marked skepticism toward the technology and its stated safety benefits. (RTRS)

Berkshire Hathaway has selected Gen Re chairman Charlie Shamieh as the successor to longtime insurance mastermind Ajit Jain, aiming to ensure a smooth leadership transition at one of the conglomerate’s most critical businesses, according to WSJ sources. (WSJ)

'Morgan Stanley’s Investment Banking Program in Budapest Hit by U.S. Probe' WSJ article notes Finra launched an inquiry asking about unlicensed junior investment bankers in Hungary working on deals for clients in the U.S. and Europe. (WSJ)

Grab Holdings Ltd. plans to adjust its Indonesian business after Jakarta’s surprise edict to lower the ride-hailing commissions it can charge, though executives expect the decree to cover just a fraction of its fleet. (BBG)

Key Nvidia Corp. partner Hon Hai Precision Industry Co. reported a 29.7% increase in April revenue, underscoring persistently strong spending on hardware essential for AI. (BBG)

China’s efforts to curb a brutal price war between its dominant solar-panel makers have started lifting prices, raising the prospect of the end of the era of ever-cheaper cells that drove surging uptake of the technology. (FT)

Volkswagen AG’s Audi warned that US President Donald Trump’s push for higher tariffs on European cars may weigh on its financial performance this year. (BBG)

Budweiser maker Anheuser-Busch InBev booked its first sales-volumes growth in three years, adding to signs of a rebound in the beer industry. (WSJ)

Shell is pushing to weaken planned rules for the production of green hydrogen in Europe, throwing its weight into an increasingly contested area of energy and climate policy about what is deemed to be “green”. (FT)

Hugo Boss confirmed its expectations for the current year, but warned that market conditions have become more challenging due to the war in the Persian Gulf. (WSJ)

HSBC Holdings’ first-quarter net profit was largely flat as higher credit charges amid the Middle East conflict offset the strength in its Hong Kong, U.K. and wealth businesses. (WSJ)

Kazakhstan said a fire broke out at Glencore Plc’s Kazzinc plant in the east of the country and has now been extinguished. (BBG)

Vodafone will take full ownership of its joint venture with CK Hutchison after the Hong Kong conglomerate agreed to sell its stake in one of the U.K.’s largest mobile operators for more than US$5 billion. (WSJ)

UniCredit lifted its guidance for the year, as its first-quarter results were boosted by strong revenue. (WSJ)

Regis Resources and Vault Minerals have agreed to combine, creating Australia’s third-largest listed gold company, valued at an estimated US$7.67 billion. (WSJ)

MAIN BUILDING NG PUP STA. MESA CAMPUS, NASUNOG

Makapal na usok ang bumalot sa isang bahagi ng Polytechnic University of the Philippines Sta. Mesa Campus - Main Academic Building, matapos ang naitalang insidente ng sunog ngayong hapon, May 5, ayon sa Facebook post ng Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP).

Ayon pa sa pahayag ng unibersidad, naapula na ang naturang sunog. Samantala, agarang sinuspinde ang in-person classes sa naturang gusali.

Paglilinaw ng PUP, hindi kabilang sa anunsiyong ito ang College of Law, CHK (night classes), Lab High and Senior High, COC, CE, ITech, M.H. Del Pilar Buildings.

Video Courtesy: Brgy. Chairman Jaime Co Jr.

CLASS SUSPENSION DAHIL SA FIRE INCIDENT

Inanunsyo ng Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP) na suspendido ang lahat ng in-person classes sa Sta. Mesa Campus - Main Academic Building dahil sa isang fire incident ngayong Martes, May 5.

“As a precautionary measure and for the safety of all students, everyone is requested to evacuate and safely exit the university premises. This is to ensure protection from possible harmful smoke or air contaminants caused by the incident.”

📸: Polytechnic University of the Philippines (Official) (Facebook)
